rationale: The student struggles with one-to-one correspondence, double-counting items without tracking. Placing counters one by one into distinct cells of a ten-frame physically structures the counting space so each object gets exactly one touch and one spot.
intent: Practice 1-to-1 placement up to 7 counters on a single 10-frame (specifically avoiding 8 to keep it distinct from the current problem), reinforcing one object per space.

data.title: Counting Objects to 10
data.description: Place counters into separate ten-frame cells one by one to practice keeping track of each counted item.

challenges.hint: Place two counters on the frame, one in each space.
challenges.narration: Let's start by placing 2 counters on the frame, one by one.
challenges.instruction: Put 2 counters on the ten frame!

challenges.hint: Try placing three counters carefully into the first row.
challenges.narration: Now, can you place 3 counters on the frame?
challenges.instruction: Put 3 counters on the ten frame!

challenges.hint: Fill four spaces with your counters.
challenges.narration: Great job! Let's put 4 counters on the frame next.
challenges.instruction: Put 4 counters on the ten frame!

challenges.hint: Fill the entire top row of five spaces.
challenges.narration: Wonderful! Can you place 5 counters to fill the whole top row?
challenges.instruction: Put 5 counters on the ten frame!

challenges.hint: Fill the top row of five, and add one more in the bottom row.
challenges.narration: Now let's count up to 6 by placing 6 counters.
challenges.instruction: Put 6 counters on the ten frame!

challenges.hint: Fill the top row and add two counters to the bottom row.
challenges.narration: You are doing fantastic! Can you place 7 counters on the frame?
challenges.instruction: Put 7 counters on the ten frame!

challenges.hint: Leave only one empty space on the entire ten-frame.
challenges.narration: For our final challenge, let's place 9 counters on the frame!
challenges.instruction: Put 9 counters on the ten frame!

judgement.reasoning: The student struggles with one-to-one correspondence and keeping track of counted items in varied/scattered arrangements. Moving to a ten-frame structure enforces one object per cell, physically and visually preventing double-counting or skipping objects. The sequence begins with small numbers (2, 3, 4) and builds up, providing a simpler structured scaffold.
judgement.verdict: This is an excellent detour because the ten-frame visually enforces one-to-one placement to fix the student's double-counting habit.
